findings.detail: The suite is thorough on the numeric edges it was written for, but it does not pin the shape of the pattern the previous commit deliberately chose. `^[+-]?(\d+(\.\d*)?|\.\d+)([eE][+-]?\d+)?$` has three branches with no test on either side of them: the leading `+` (`'+5'`), the bare-fraction alternative `\.\d+` (`'.5'`), and the trailing-dot form `'5.'`. A rejection case is also unpinned — `'1e'` and `'1e+'` are non-numeric only because `[eE][+-]?\d+` requires at least one exponent digit. Because the alternation exists specifically to keep the match unambiguous, the realistic future edit is someone 'simplifying' it back toward `^\d+(\.\d+)?([eE]...)?$` — which reintroduces nothing that fails here, yet silently reclassifies `.5` and `+5` as `non-numeric` and hands a Composite Check user 'Non-numeric Qty' for a real half-kilo. The long-digit-run test at line 106 guards the backtracking half of the regex's design; nothing guards the accepted-shape half.
findings.summary: Three regex alternation branches are unasserted, so a future simplification passes silently
